Synopsis:
A Climate Council report projects $855.1bn in economic losses across Australia by 2100 due to rising sea levels and coastal flooding. Over 267,000 properties and 2m hectares of land are at risk, with Queensland, NSW and WA most exposed. Agricultural viability is threatened across ~620,000 hectares of farmland, raising food security concerns. The analysis uses RCP4.5 scenario (+2.7°C by 2100) and is grounded in peer-reviewed modelling. The report urges immediate adaptation planning.
